The protective quality of the IZO/TCC encapsulant was evaluated by subjecting PSCs to aging conditions of continuous illumination under quasi-MPP tracking in air at 50˚C, 40-60% R.H. As shown in Figure 6d, Encapsulated PSCs demonstrated noteworthy improvements in operational lifetimes, with the champion PSC maintaining over 90% of its initial PCE of 21.65% for 1,430 hours (T90 of 1,430 hours). These reports show a wide range of aging conditions (e.g., storage in N , in 2 ambient air, in air at 85˚C 85% R.H., MPP light-soaking) for various encapsulation materials (e.g., polymers, inorganic single and multilayer systems, in-grain encapsulation). Within the broad context of this sample population, outstanding stabilities are only attained in a controlled environment (i.e., dry air, dark), which is significantly reduced when identical devices are aged under illumination with MPP tracking.92 As such, it is important to account for aging conditions when comparing stability metrics across studies.93 To this effect, data points were filtered to 14 devices reported across 10 publications that measure the operational lifetimes of PSCs by aging under conditions comparable to the ones used in our study (i.e., continuous illumination in ambient air and MPP tracking). Under these conditions, our result (PCE 21.65%: T90 of 1,430 hours) demonstrates the highest performance amongst thin-film encapsulated PSCs (Figure 7), on par with the historical trend of operational lifetimes achieved with all encapsulation techniques.3 With the prospect of optimizing TCC characteristics (e.g., optical transparency, electrical conductivity) and architecture (e.g., number of dyads, TCO properties), our proposed innovation has the potential to facilitate advanced encapsulation strategies for the benefit of solar conversion devices. For example, when implemented in conjunction with a cover glass for PV systems, it allows for relocating the grid away from the device to the glass cover, thereby permitting a hermetic seal of the PV device by the thin-film encapsulant and preventing ingress through protruding grids.
